classification.summary: Curve.flash() was the only state-changing entry point without the contract's nonReentrant guard, so the attacker re-entered deposit() inside flashCallback and had the flash-loaned XIDR/USDC counted both as flash repayment and as a new LP deposit, then withdrew the underlying.

loss.notes: Migrated from legacy lossUsd/lossOther. The legacy corpus did not consistently distinguish gross from net loss or record valuation provenance.

sources.note: onchain review: verified Curve source on 0x46161158b1947d9149e066d6d31af1283b2d377c - every other mutating function carries nonReentrant, flash() does not; victim created by 0xa75ceb6801d48449affa0ee6f31205b2a5567bec (DFX deployer) in tx 0xdf81dad568a455c860bfd7defb2861a4699b896e31c6c1c49836cd5bb10362fb, unrelated to attack sender 0x14c19962e4a899f29b3dd9ff52ebfb5e4cb9a067; no EIP-1967 Upgraded events before the incident. Recheck (deployment basis confirmed): keccak(eth_getCode) on the Curve is identical at the creation block 15747623 and the incident block 15941704, and it is not a proxy (implementation() reverts; Etherscan's Proxy flag is a false positive). Of the code executed in its context during the exploit, the Swaps library 0x5fca000f8a1ef45fe2412a8e305ff36d8757be0f is a PUSH20 link-time constant in the runtime, and the two assimilators it delegatecalls, 0x08cd9d993840cca86546f4ebf166c78c7d8ff700 and 0xc2e645c253faf984b6af2668798719b7c6abab95, live in curve.assets[0] and [1] (slots keccak(4) and keccak(4)+1); binary-searching eth_getStorageAt on both over [15747623, 15941703] shows they were written at deployment and never changed.
